text: Degree conditions; Hierholzer.

An Euler path (欧拉路径) uses every edge exactly once; an Euler circuit also ends where it started. Undirected graph: a circuit exists iff all degrees are even (and the edges are connected); a path iff exactly 0 or 2 vertices have odd degree, starting at one of them. Directed: in = out everywhere for a circuit; for a path, one vertex has out = in + 1 (the start) and one has in = out + 1.

Hierholzer's algorithm: DFS along unused edges; when a vertex has no unused edge left, push it onto the answer. The answer read backwards is the Euler path. Each edge is used once: O(m), with a pointer per vertex to the next unused edge.

Lexicographically smallest directed Euler path (P7771): sort each adjacency list and start at the vertex with out = in + 1 (or vertex 1). Checking path.size() == m + 1 catches graphs whose edges are not all connected.

Recursion depth can reach m; for m ≈ 10⁶ write the DFS with an explicit stack. For undirected graphs, mark each edge used by its id, because it appears in two adjacency lists (P2731 Riding the Fences, P1341).
Deque: 0 edges front, 1 edges back.

0-1 BFS: when every edge weight is 0 or 1, use a deque instead of Dijkstra's heap. A 0-edge puts the neighbour at the front (same distance), a 1-edge at the back. The deque stays sorted by distance, so it is Dijkstra in O(n + m).
Typical: grids where some moves are free and others cost one (break a wall, turn, change colour), and "minimum number of special edges" on any graph.
Fewest walls to break from the top-left to the bottom-right corner. Checked against Dijkstra written in Python.
Unlike plain BFS, a cell can be improved after it was first reached, so check dist again (as above) instead of a visited flag (P4554).
Merge nodes; bottleneck = LCA value.

The Kruskal reconstruction tree (Kruskal 重构树): run Kruskal, but whenever an edge of weight w joins two components, create a new node with value w and make both component roots its children. The result is a binary tree whose leaves are the original vertices, and values grow towards the root.

The smallest possible "largest edge" on a path between a and b equals the value of LCA(a, b) in this tree. All vertices reachable from v using only edges ≤ x form one subtree: climb from v while the parent's value ≤ x (binary lifting). That makes "reachable within a limit" queries online (归程 P4768).
Answers checked in Python by adding edges in weight order until a and b connect. The tree has 2n − 1 nodes; leaves have value 0.
Compared with 货车运输(进阶篇第11章), which stored the bottleneck on binary-lifting jumps, this turns the bottleneck into a single LCA value and also gives the whole reachable set as a subtree.
Two-colouring; odd cycles.

A graph is bipartite (二分图) iff it can be 2-coloured so every edge joins different colours, iff it has no odd cycle. Check by BFS or DFS colouring each component: a conflict (an edge inside one colour) proves an odd cycle.
Each component can be coloured in exactly two ways (swap the colours). Problems often ask for the better of the two per component (P1330: guard the fewest nodes so every edge has exactly one guard).
Impossible
A triangle is an odd cycle: Impossible. The path 1–2–3 colours as 0, 1, 0: guarding {2} (one node) or {1, 3} (two); take 1.
Alternatives: DSU with "enemy" copies (关押罪犯 P1525 binary searches the answer and checks bipartiteness); weighted DSU storing parity to the root, which also handles edges arriving one by one.
